title: Recruitment Consultant Salary: Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Recruitment Consultant Salary

A recruitment consultant salary in Australia can vary widely depending on the employer, location, experience, and whether the role is permanent or casual. According to the Fair Work Ombudsman, most recruitment consultants are not covered by an award. This means their minimum pay is the National Minimum Wage, unless their employer is in the labour market assistance industry or they perform mainly clerical work. The [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, bringing the casual minimum to $33.05 per hour.

Many recruitment consultants earn above the minimum, especially those with commission structures or in high-demand sectors. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings across all occupations average $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). For recruitment consultants specifically, the median weekly earnings are not published at the six-digit occupation level, but the Jobs and Skills Australia profile notes that 83% work full-time, with average full-time hours of 41 per week. However, for standard pay calculations, we use 38 hours as the benchmark.

### Award Coverage for Recruitment Consultants

The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that award coverage depends on the employer and duties. If you work for a recruitment agency that is not in the labour market assistance industry, you are likely award-free. This means your minimum entitlement is the National Minimum Wage and the National Employment Standards (NES). If you work for an employer in the labour market assistance industry (providing job placement services under government contracts), you are covered by the Labour Market Assistance Award. That award has specific classification levels and minimum rates. If your role is primarily clerical or administrative, the Clerks Award may apply. Otherwise, the Miscellaneous Award could cover you if you are not a professional employee. Professional employees (those requiring a degree, such as a bachelor’s in human resources) are generally award-free.

Because most recruitment consultants are award-free, your pay is negotiated between you and your employer. The [pay guides](/blog) from Fair Work are useful for award-covered roles, but for award-free roles the National Minimum Wage is the floor.

## Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

A key feature of the recruitment consultant salary landscape is the treatment of casual loading and superannuation. Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on their base hourly rate. This loading is intended to compensate for the lack of paid leave (annual leave, personal leave) and other entitlements that permanent employees receive. When using the [timesheet](/) on this site, you enter your base hourly rate, and if you are casual, you check the casual loading box. The displayed rate then includes the 25% loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary time earnings. For casual employees, ordinary earnings include the casual loading. So if your base rate is $30.00 per hour and you are casual, your loaded rate is $37.50 per hour, and super is calculated on that $37.50. The employer pays super on top, meaning your total cost to the employer is $37.50 + 12% ($4.50) = $42.00 per hour. The super guarantee has a maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27; earnings above that do not attract compulsory super. You can read more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Calculating Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, we assume 38 hours per week, as this is the standard for the National Minimum Wage and most awards. For example, a recruitment consultant earning $35.00 per hour (base) working 38 hours per week would have an annual salary of $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160. If they are casual, the loaded rate of $43.75 per hour gives $43.75 × 38 × 52 = $86,450. This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

You can also think in fortnightly terms: weekly pay × 2. For the $35.00 base rate example, weekly pay is $1,330.00, so fortnightly is $2,660.00 before tax and super.

### Tax on Your Recruitment Consultant Salary

Once you have your gross annual figure, you can estimate tax using the 2026–27 resident tax rates. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Then:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator on this site can help you estimate net pay after tax and Medicare.

## Using the Timesheet for Your Recruitment Consultant Salary

The [timesheet](/) on this site is designed for anyone who wants to convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, or weekly figures. Simply type your base hourly rate. If you are a casual recruitment consultant, tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25%. The tool will then show your loaded rate, annual gross, and estimated super and tax. Remember that super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings, so the annual figure shown includes the super contribution from your employer. The tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident rates and Medicare levy.

For award-free recruitment consultants, the National Minimum Wage is the starting point, but your actual rate may be higher. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data from the ABS can give you a sense of typical earnings, but remember that recruitment consultant salaries are not published at a detailed level. Use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to compare different rates and understand the impact of casual loading.

## Key Takeaways

- Most recruitment consultants are award-free and entitled to at least the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026).
- Casual recruitment consultants receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate.
- Superannuation is 12% of ordinary earnings (including casual loading) and is paid on top by the employer.
- Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, with 38 hours as the standard full-time week.
- Use the [timesheet](/) to estimate your annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, including tax and super.

Understanding your recruitment consultant salary involves knowing your award status, whether you are casual or permanent, and how super and tax apply. The tools on this site are designed to give you a clear estimate based on the information you provide.
